VERIDANE - INTERNAL - Product Safety Committee memo PSC-2026-07
Date: 2 Oct 2026     From: Elena Kowalczyk, VP Quality & Product Safety     To: Executive Leadership Team

Subject: GV-400 series combination gas valve - voluntary recall (CPSC Fast Track)

Summary
- Affected units: ~41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves, date codes 2507-2612, sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters.
- Issue: diaphragm seat can deform under sustained high-inlet-pressure conditions, allowing gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. 17 field reports of gas odor; 2 reports of delayed ignition causing cabinet damage; no injuries reported.
- Root cause: change of diaphragm compound supplier (Q1 2025); supplier lot material out of spec on compression set. Corrective action complete; replacement valves shipping from Mequon plant since 28 Sep.
- Regulatory: CPSC Fast Track filed 22 Sep; joint recall notice expected the week of 19 Oct. Canada (Health Canada) notification filed.
- Cost: reserve booked in Q3 $21.6M (field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement, logistics). Range $18-26M. Supplier recovery claim of ~$9M lodged, not recognised.
- Customer impact: three OEMs (incl. our 2nd-largest BCV customer) have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice. Included in updated guidance.

These conditions raise substantial doubt about the Company's ability to continue as a going concern. [Management's plans paragraph - to be provided by the Company. Whether the plans alleviate substantial doubt will be considered at the issuance date.]

## Quarter ended September 30, 2026 | To be released Thursday, November 5, 2026, 4:05 p.m. ET

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Data-center cooling was the story of the third quarter. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) grew net sales 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, we won two new hyperscale awards, and total backlog finished the quarter at a record $918.0 million, up 13.0%. TDC backlog of $574.2 million is up 22.0% and now represents 62.5% of company backlog. That is the growth engine of this company, and it is accelerating.

Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin, and adjusted EPS was $0.15. On a GAAP basis, the quarter produced a net loss of $15.6 million, or $(0.37) per diluted share, which includes a $21.6 million recall charge and $6.2 million of restructuring costs. The KPI table accompanying this release sets out the full GAAP results and the reconciliations to our non-GAAP measures.

## Highlights

- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, with two new hyperscale awards won in the quarter.
- Record total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year; TDC backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0%.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million; adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- GV-400 root cause identified, corrective action completed, and replacement valves shipping from our Mequon plant since September 28.
- Project Keystone launched, targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** Net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4%. Momentum is broadening across hyperscale, colocation and enterprise customers, and the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger we launched in the second quarter is ramping with its initial hyperscale customers. The two hyperscale awards won this quarter extend our revenue visibility well into FY2027. TDC backlog ended the quarter at $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year, and now represents 62.5% of company backlog. Our customers are investing in liquid cooling as rack densities rise, and we are investing alongside them — in products, in capacity, and in the engineering resources that keep us qualified at the largest data-center operators in the market.

**Building Controls & Valves.** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9%, reflecting softer commercial construction activity and lower shipments into commercial HVAC and unit heater production. In addition, three OEM customers — including our second-largest BCV customer — have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice. That pause is captured in our updated guidance, and we are working closely with these customers to resume orders as the recall notice is issued and replacement supply ramps.

Underneath the quarter's shipments, BCV backlog was essentially flat at $343.8 million, up 0.6% year over year. We read that as a signal that the underlying book-and-ship business is holding even while current-period revenue softens.

**GV-400 recall.** On September 22, we filed a Fast Track recall with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission covering approximately 41,200 GV-400 and GV-410 combination gas valves sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters, with date codes 2507 through 2612. This was a voluntary, proactive, customer-first action. We identified the root cause — a supplier lot of diaphragm compound that was out of specification on compression set — completed the corrective action, and began shipping replacement valves from our Mequon plant on September 28. The joint recall notice with the CPSC is expected the week of October 19, and the corresponding Health Canada notification has been filed. *[Drafting note: the CPSC notice will have been published before the 5 November release — update this sentence to past tense and confirm details against the published notice.]* We recorded a reserve of $21.6 million in the third quarter to cover field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement and logistics. We have also lodged a supplier recovery claim; no recovery benefit has been recognized in the quarter.

**Project Keystone.** We are moving with equal speed on cost. Keystone targets $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of the second quarter of FY2027, spanning procurement, manufacturing footprint and overhead, and it is designed to make the company structurally more profitable as TDC volumes ramp. We recorded $6.2 million of restructuring costs in the quarter as the program gets underway.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year FY2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion, from $1.78–1.84 billion, and to adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million, from $255–270 million. The update reflects lower BCV volumes, the pause in GV-400 orders pending the recall notice, and the recall charge itself. Two things do not change: TDC's growth trajectory as record backlog converts to revenue, and the $35 million of Keystone savings we intend to realize by the end of Q2 FY2027. We expect TDC to remain our growth engine into FY2027, supported by the hyperscale awards won this quarter and the order visibility that comes with a backlog of this size. We will provide FY2027 guidance with our fourth-quarter results. In the meantime we are managing what we can control: capital expenditures were $14.9 million in the quarter, and working capital and discretionary spending are being managed tightly across both segments.

As of September 30, 2026, we were not in compliance with the financial maintenance covenants under our credit agreement. We have requested a waiver and amendment from our lenders and are in active discussions with the bank group. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Further detail will be included in our Form 10-Q.

## Closing

To our employees — particularly the quality, engineering and plant teams in Mequon who moved from root cause to shipping replacement valves in a matter of weeks — thank you. To our OEM customers, who have worked alongside us on the recall, thank you for your partnership. We are executing with urgency on the things within our control: converting a record backlog, delivering the Keystone savings, completing the recall with the speed and care our customers expect, and rebuilding our margins and our balance sheet as we do it.

# Veridane Fluid Technologies — Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders
## Quarter ended September 30, 2026 | To be released Thursday, November 5, 2026, 4:05 p.m. ET

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Data-center cooling was the story of the third quarter. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) grew net sales 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, we won two new hyperscale awards, and total backlog finished the quarter at a record $918.0 million, up 13.0%. TDC backlog of $574.2 million is up 22.0% and now represents 62.5% of company backlog. That is the growth engine of this company, and it is accelerating.

Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin, and adjusted EPS was $0.15. On a GAAP basis, the quarter produced a net loss of $15.6 million, or $(0.37) per diluted share, which includes the GV-400 recall charge and Project Keystone restructuring costs. The KPI table accompanying this release sets out the full GAAP results, the charge amounts, and the reconciliations to our non-GAAP measures.

## Highlights

- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, with two new hyperscale awards won in the quarter.
- Record total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year; TDC backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0%.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million; adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- GV-400 root cause identified, corrective action completed, and replacement valves shipping from our Mequon plant since September 28.
- Project Keystone launched, targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** Net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4%. Momentum is broadening across hyperscale, colocation and enterprise customers, and the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger we launched in the second quarter is ramping with its initial hyperscale customers. The two hyperscale awards won this quarter extend our revenue visibility well into FY2027. TDC backlog ended the quarter at $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year, and now represents 62.5% of company backlog. Our customers are investing in liquid cooling as rack densities rise, and we are investing alongside them — in products, in capacity, and in the engineering resources that keep us qualified at the largest data-center operators in the market.

**Building Controls & Valves.** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9%, reflecting softer commercial construction activity and lower shipments into commercial HVAC and unit heater production. In addition, three OEM customers — including our second-largest BCV customer — have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice. That pause is captured in our updated guidance, and we are working closely with these customers to resume orders as the recall notice is issued and replacement supply ramps.

Underneath the quarter's shipments, BCV backlog was essentially flat at $343.8 million, up 0.6% year over year. We read that as a signal that the underlying book-and-ship business is holding even while current-period revenue softens.

**GV-400 recall.** On September 22, we filed a Fast Track recall with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission covering approximately 41,200 GV-400 and GV-410 combination gas valves sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters, with date codes 2507 through 2612. This was a voluntary, proactive, customer-first action. We identified the root cause — a supplier lot of diaphragm compound that was out of specification on compression set — completed the corrective action, and began shipping replacement valves from our Mequon plant on September 28. The joint recall notice with the CPSC is expected the week of October 19, and the corresponding Health Canada notification has been filed. *[Drafting note: the CPSC notice will have been published before the 5 November release — update this sentence to past tense and confirm details against the published notice.]* We recorded a reserve of $21.6 million in the third quarter to cover field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement and logistics. We have also lodged a supplier recovery claim; no recovery benefit has been recognized in the quarter.

**Project Keystone.** We are moving with equal speed on cost. Keystone targets $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of the second quarter of FY2027, spanning procurement, manufacturing footprint and overhead, and it is designed to make the company structurally more profitable as TDC volumes ramp. We recorded $6.2 million of restructuring costs in the quarter as the program gets underway.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year FY2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion, from $1.78–1.84 billion, and to adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million, from $255–270 million. The update reflects lower BCV volumes, the pause in GV-400 orders pending the recall notice, and the recall charge itself. Two things do not change: TDC's growth trajectory as record backlog converts to revenue, and the $35 million of Keystone savings we intend to realize by the end of Q2 FY2027. We expect TDC to remain our growth engine into FY2027, supported by the hyperscale awards won this quarter and the order visibility that comes with a backlog of this size. We will provide FY2027 guidance with our fourth-quarter results. In the meantime we are managing what we can control: capital expenditures were $14.9 million in the quarter, and working capital and discretionary spending are being managed tightly across both segments.

As of September 30, 2026, we were not in compliance with the financial maintenance covenants under our credit agreement. We have requested a waiver and amendment from our lenders and are in active discussions with the bank group. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Further detail will be included in our Form 10-Q.

## Closing

To our employees — particularly the quality, engineering and plant teams in Mequon who moved from root cause to shipping replacement valves in a matter of weeks — thank you. To our OEM customers, who have worked alongside us on the recall, thank you for your partnership. We are executing with urgency on the things within our control: converting a record backlog, delivering the Keystone savings, completing the recall with the speed and care our customers expect, and rebuilding our margins and our balance sheet as we do it.

Dana Whitcombe, President & Chief Executive Officer

Mark Ostrander, EVP & Chief Financial Officer
